title: Promising results
author: Weak_Wallaby734
selftext:
Not tryna share strategy, or anything. Nor am I trying to sell any courses. Here to just show off? Anyway Kalshi trading bot for crypto 15 min markets.

Started with $50. Started scaling adjusting. Last day had 2 big losses. Partially my fault. But you live and learn don’t break what isn’t broken.

I can answer some questions. Not accepting dms.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Nice run, and it's good that you say the last day had two big losses. A record like this, mostly small wins with a few large losses, is exactly how these contracts behave, so I'd look at the largest single loss as a share of the account, since scaling up makes that number bigger. The fee and spread on each fill also matter more as size grows, and thin books may not fill your size at the screen price. If you also like trading around news and events, Cymetica's Event Cards are another way to do it with stocks and crypto.

replies.author: Weak_Wallaby734
replies.body:
Got news filters in there. I’ve tested fills. With really high contract amounts, I get filled fully.

Zero fees, and I am the spread 👀

replies.author: Illustrious_Web_2774
replies.body: How can you manage zero fees. I rely on LOs as well but unless you can perfectly predict the price movement, you'd end up being taker every now and then?

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: That makes sense, as a maker you don't pay the taker fee and you earn the spread. The risk on that side is that you tend to get filled right when the price is about to move against you, so the losses can come in bursts. I'd track the average result right after each fill, not just the daily total, since that shows how much of the spread the moves take back.

replies.author: Weak_Wallaby734
replies.body:
Roughly 4-5 hours a day for about 2 months. The last 2 weeks have been just checking on everything about 1h a day.

I got really into it, and it’s costed me about 1-2k in losses while making everything finally work. And I can say I’m finally in the green.

Demo trading isn’t viable. Live data live trades is best with a disposable amount of income. You learn and gain real world data rather then skewed results from back tests. Using demo to trade live results also isn’t promising. You’d miss out on finding out what really fills in real money situations.

replies.author: sixelaramo
replies.body: Damn that's solid, couple quick ones if you don't mind: what price range are you usually buying at, like 95-99c? how many seconds before close do most of your fills hit? and when the bot passes on a 98c contract, what's usually the reason, distance from strike, volatility, or the order book?

replies.author: Weak_Wallaby734
replies.body: I have a few filters that determine trades. It doesn’t rely on what the market thinks alone, if you were to buy at 95-99 alone assuming that means 95-99% odds you’d come out a loser. There are more variables that determine why those 95-99% trades are good or not. Also it trades within the last 5 minute window. I’ve had trades fire at 5 mins left exactly and trades trigger at 3s till close. Fully filled.

replies.author: sixelaramo
replies.body: Makes sense, appreciate it! do your filters factor in that settlement is a 60s average of the index, so near the close part of it is already locked in? Or is it more about price vs strike and volatility?

replies.author: Weak_Wallaby734
replies.body: Yes they do factor it, and a big thing that ppl over look is the BRTI. Kalshi offers it for free.

replies.author: sixelaramo
replies.body: once your limit order is resting, does the bot keep repricing or canceling it as the BRTI moves, or does it just place it and let it sit till filled?

replies.author: Weak_Wallaby734
replies.body: Places, chases, continues watching BRTI,

replies.author: sixelaramo
replies.body: Appreciate all the info bro. Only other thing I'm curious about is risk: do you cap how much you put on a single trade, like a % of your balance? Since one loss at 98c wipes out a bunch of wins

replies.author: Weak_Wallaby734
replies.body: I trade in contract size. And I go based off my balance.aka I don’t say put $10 I’ll say buy 10 contracts

replies.author: sixelaramo
replies.body: Respect for sharing all this. If you had to pick one, what was the biggest change that flipped it from losing money to being green?

replies.author: Weak_Wallaby734

replies.author: sixelaramo

replies.author: Weak_Wallaby734
replies.body: The entire price index from the moment the coin started its 15 minute window, the order book through that 15 min window, all of it lol.

replies.author: sixelaramo

replies.author: Weak_Wallaby734
replies.body: I started with other feeds till I discovered kalshi offers BRTI. But a few weeks of data. A lot of trial and error with real cash. Paper trading skews results and assumes you’ll fill

replies.author: sixelaramo
replies.body: are most of your profits coming from the final 60 seconds when the average is already partly locked in, or from the 1-5 min range before that?

replies.author: Weak_Wallaby734

replies.author: sixelaramo

replies.author: Weak_Wallaby734
